statement: Around 45% of dementia worldwide is attributable to 14 modifiable risk factors acting across the life course; eliminating or reducing them could in principle prevent or delay that share of cases at the population level.
effect_size: PAF ~45% across 14 factors (2024); was ~40% across 12 factors (2020). Largest single factors: hearing loss 7%, high LDL 7%, less education 5%, social isolation 5%.
population: Lancet standing Commission synthesis of global observational evidence (meta of cohorts + prevalence weighting)

provenance.primary: Livingston et al. - 'Dementia prevention, intervention, and care: 2024 report of the Lancet standing Commission', Lancet 2024 (2020 report: 10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30367-6)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: The spine of dementia prevention. PAF is a POPULATION counterfactual, NOT a personal risk reduction (predictor != lever). The PAFs are weighted for factor overlap and rest LARGELY on observational risk estimates; only a few factors (hearing, vascular, multidomain lifestyle) have randomized prevention support. The ~55% remainder is non-modifiable/unknown (age, APOE4, unknown causes).

statement: Greater baseline hearing-loss severity is associated with higher incident dementia risk in a dose-dependent manner.
effect_size: Hazard rising with severity: mild/moderate/severe hearing loss ~ 2x / 3x / 5x dementia risk vs normal hearing
population: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, n~639, baseline age 36-90

provenance.primary: Lin, Metter, O'Brien et al. - 'Hearing Loss and Incident Dementia', Arch Neurol 2011
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Strong observational signal but cannot separate cause from marker (hearing loss could be an early sign of the same neurodegeneration). The causal test is ACHIEVE (separate claim).

statement: A hearing intervention (hearing aids + audiologic support) did NOT significantly slow 3-year cognitive decline in the full cohort, but slowed decline by ~48% in the prespecified higher-risk subgroup.
effect_size: Full cohort: null (no significant difference). At-risk (ARIC) subgroup: ~48% slower 3-year global cognitive decline vs control
population: 977 adults aged 70-84 with untreated mild-to-moderate hearing loss; ~half from the higher-risk ARIC cardiovascular cohort

provenance.primary: Lin et al. - 'Hearing intervention versus health education control to reduce cognitive decline in older adults with hearing loss in the USA (ACHIEVE)', Lancet 2023
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: The field's best recent CAUSAL evidence that treating a single factor can protect cognition - but the primary endpoint was NULL overall and the striking 48% is a subgroup. Honest read: reasonable and low-risk to treat hearing loss; overstatement to say 'hearing aids prevent dementia' full-stop.

statement: Intensive blood-pressure control (target <120 mmHg systolic) significantly reduced mild cognitive impairment and the combined MCI-or-dementia endpoint versus standard control; the dementia-alone endpoint missed significance.
effect_size: Significant reduction in MCI and MCI-or-dementia composite; dementia-alone hazard reduced but not statistically significant (trial stopped early, underpowered for the rarer endpoint)
population: SPRINT hypertension trial cognition substudy, n~9,361 hypertensive adults >=50

provenance.primary: Williamson et al. (SPRINT MIND Investigators) - 'Effect of Intensive vs Standard Blood Pressure Control on Probable Dementia', JAMA 2019

confidence_notes: Best randomized evidence that a vascular lever moves a COGNITIVE outcome. Dementia-alone null is a power artifact (early stop for CV benefit), not evidence of no effect. Supports the vascular cluster of the Lancet PAF table.

statement: A year of moderate aerobic exercise increased hippocampal volume ~2% (reversing 1-2 years of age-related shrinkage) and improved spatial memory, with BDNF as a mediator.
effect_size: ~2% increase in anterior hippocampus volume vs ~1.4% decline in stretching control; improved spatial memory; BDNF mediation
population: 120 older adults (avg 67y), 1-year aerobic-exercise vs stretching RCT

provenance.primary: Erickson et al. - 'Exercise training increases size of hippocampus and improves memory', PNAS 2011
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Strong MECHANISM/surrogate (imaging) result. Does NOT establish the OUTCOME 'exercise prevents dementia' - RCTs of exercise on cognitive decline in MCI/older adults are MIXED-to-null. Mechanism solid, fitness predicts cognition strongly, but the prevention outcome is not settled.

statement: A 2-year multidomain lifestyle intervention (diet + exercise + cognitive training + vascular monitoring) preserved cognition versus general health advice in at-risk older adults - the first RCT to show this.
effect_size: Intervention group composite cognitive (NTB) score improved ~25% more than control over 2 years; executive function and processing speed effects larger
population: FINGER trial, 1260 at-risk Finns aged 60-77, normal-to-slightly-impaired cognition

provenance.primary: Ngandu et al. - 'A 2 year multidomain intervention ... to prevent cognitive decline in at-risk elderly people (FINGER): a randomised controlled trial', Lancet 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Proof-of-concept that bundled lifestyle CAN move cognition in an RCT. Outcome is cognitive TEST performance, not dementia diagnosis; effect modest; control also got lighter advice. World-Wide FINGERS network now replicating (US-POINTER etc.) - generalization still open.

statement: Higher MIND/Mediterranean diet adherence is associated with slower cognitive decline and lower Alzheimer's risk in cohorts, but a 3-year RCT found no significant cognitive benefit of the MIND diet over a control diet.
effect_size: Cohort: MIND adherence assoc. with ~53% lower AD risk (top vs bottom tertile, Morris 2015). RCT: both arms improved cognition, no significant between-group difference (Barnes 2023)
population: Cohort: Rush Memory and Aging Project, n~923. RCT: 604 older adults at risk, 3 years, both arms with mild caloric restriction

provenance.primary: Barnes et al. - 'Trial of the MIND Diet for Prevention of Cognitive Decline in Older Persons', NEJM 2023 (cohort: Morris et al., Alzheimers Dement 2015, 10.1016/j.jalz.2015.04.007)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Textbook predictor-vs-lever / cohort-vs-RCT case: strong observational signal did NOT survive randomization. Caveats: both RCT arms lost weight and improved (control was not a junk-food arm); 3y may be too short. Honest grade: reasonable heart-healthy pattern, strong cohort signal, null RCT for cognition.

statement: Depression is associated with roughly 1.5-2x higher all-cause mortality, and is a bidirectional dementia risk factor (cause and early symptom).
effect_size: ~1.5-2x all-cause mortality (meta-analyses); Lancet dementia PAF for depression ~3%

provenance.primary: Cuijpers & Smit - 'Excess mortality in depression: a meta-analysis of community studies', J Affect Disord 2002 (10.1016/S0165-0327(01)00413-X); Lancet Commission 2024 for dementia PAF
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; cross-ref Domain M

confidence_notes: Real and important but causally tangled - reverse causation strong for the dementia link (depression is an early symptom of incipient neurodegeneration). Cross-ref Domain M psychosocial determinants.

statement: Exercise is an effective treatment for depression (walking/jogging, yoga, strength training, mixed aerobic all beneficial), with larger effects at higher intensity.
effect_size: Moderate-to-large reductions in depression; effects rival/approach psychotherapy and medication in head-to-head arms; effects shrink but stay positive in lowest-bias studies

provenance.primary: Noetel et al. - 'Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials', BMJ 2024
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: One of the cleaner INTERVENTIONAL mental-health stories. Authors flag most included trials have HIGH risk of bias and effects attenuate in low-bias studies - but stay positive. A real, RCT-supported lever.

statement: There is no consistent evidence that depression is caused by low serotonin; the 'chemical imbalance' narrative is not supported - which does NOT negate the modest, RCT-proven efficacy of antidepressants.
effect_size: Umbrella review: no consistent low-serotonin signal in depression. Separately, antidepressant efficacy SMD ~0.30 vs placebo (Cipriani 2018) - small-to-moderate, larger in severe depression
population: Moncrieff: umbrella review of systematic reviews. Cipriani: network meta of 522 trials, 116,477 participants, 21 antidepressants

provenance.primary: Moncrieff et al. - 'The serotonin theory of depression: a systematic umbrella review', Mol Psychiatry 2022 (10.1038/s41380-022-01661-0); Cipriani et al., Lancet 2018 (10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32802-7)

confidence_notes: Hold two things at once: the serotonin-deficiency MECHANISM/marketing story is false, AND antidepressants have modest real OUTCOME efficacy. A drug can work without the folk-mechanism being true - the schema's mechanism-vs-outcome rule exactly.

statement: Dietary improvement (Mediterranean-style) produced significantly greater remission of major depression than social support over 12 weeks.
population: SMILES trial, n=67 adults with major depression, single-site, unblinded

provenance.primary: Jacka et al. - 'A randomised controlled trial of dietary improvement for adults with major depression (the SMILES trial)', BMC Medicine 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Encouraging FIRST RCT for 'food as treatment' but small (n=67), single, unblinded (can't blind a diet), not robustly replicated at scale. Promising, not settled.

statement: Herpes zoster (shingles) vaccination reduced new dementia diagnoses, demonstrated via a date-of-birth eligibility cutoff that approximates randomization (natural experiment).
effect_size: Vaccination reduced 7-year dementia diagnosis by ~3.5 percentage points (~20% relative reduction), stronger in women (Wales). Recombinant Shingrix: ~17% more diagnosis-free time over 6y vs live vaccine (Taquet)
population: Wales population around the 2 Sept 1933 eligibility birthdate cutoff (regression-discontinuity natural experiment); replicated in Canada

provenance.primary: Eyting, Geldsetzer et al. - 'A natural experiment on the effect of herpes zoster vaccination on dementia', Nature 2025; Taquet et al., Nat Med 2024 (10.1038/s41591-024-03201-5); Pomirchy et al., Lancet Neurol 2026 (10.1016/S1474-4422(25)00455-7)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex search verified

confidence_notes: QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL (natural experiment / regression-discontinuity) - much stronger than typical observation because the birthdate cutoff is as-good-as-random, and now replicated in Canada. But NOT a randomized prevention trial; residual confounding (who gets vaccinated) not fully excluded; mechanism (zoster reactivation -> neuroinflammation? off-target immune training?) unresolved. One of the most interesting leads in dementia prevention - flag loudly, grade carefully. Tagged case-control as the nearest ladder rung; design is stronger than ordinary case-control.

statement: Lecanemab slowed cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's by a statistically significant but clinically marginal amount, with meaningful risks (brain edema/microhemorrhage).
effect_size: CDR-SB decline 1.21 (lecanemab) vs 1.66 (placebo) over 18 months = -0.45 points (~27% relative slowing) on an 18-point scale - at/below most minimal clinically important difference estimates. ARIA-E ~12.6%, ARIA-H ~17.3%, infusion reactions ~26%; deaths in extension esp. with anticoagulants / APOE4 homozygotes
population: CLARITY-AD, 1795 people with early Alzheimer's disease, 18 months

provenance.primary: van Dyck et al. - 'Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease', NEJM 2023 (donanemab: Sims et al., JAMA 2023, 10.1001/jama.2023.13239)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Statistically significant != clinically meaningful. Everyone still declined; drug group declined slightly less. 0.45/18 points is likely imperceptible to patients/families over 18 months, against real ARIA risk, infusion burden, MRI monitoring, and high cost. A scientific milestone (amyloid removal modestly slows decline) and a marginal clinical tool. Donanemab tells the same story.

statement: Cognitive/brain-training improves the trained task durably but shows limited transfer to untrained abilities and everyday function; commercial brain games lack evidence of improving general cognition.
effect_size: ACTIVE: durable gains in TRAINED domain at 10 years; far-transfer limited. Consensus: little evidence brain games improve general cognition/daily life beyond the games. FTC fined Lumos Labs $2M (2016) for deceptive dementia-prevention claims
population: ACTIVE RCT, 2832 older adults, 10-year follow-up; Simons et al. 2016 expert consensus review

provenance.primary: Rebok et al. - 'Ten-Year Effects of the ACTIVE Cognitive Training Trial', JAGS 2014; Simons et al., Psychol Sci Public Interest 2016 (10.1177/1529100616661983)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-8 brain brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Near-transfer real (you get good at the practiced task); far-transfer weak. The speed-of-processing arm's later dementia signal (Edwards 2017) is contested. Commercial brain-training is mostly marketing - FTC enforcement is the honest tell.

statement: Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus) produced transient cognitive improvement in a tiny short RCT that reversed after stopping; not replicated at scale.
effect_size: Improved cognitive scores during 16 weeks of supplementation in MCI; benefit reversed by 4 weeks after cessation
population: Mori et al., n~30 older Japanese adults with mild cognitive impairment, single-site

provenance.primary: Mori et al. - 'Improving effects of the mushroom Yamabushitake (Hericium erinaceus) on mild cognitive impairment: a double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial', Phytother Res 2009

confidence_notes: Tiny (n~30), short, single-site, never replicated at scale; effect reversed on stopping. Animal NGF/mechanistic data is interesting but human OUTCOME data is thin. Representative of the 'brain supplement' tier - mechanism or marketing, not proven prevention.

statement: Ginkgo biloba did not prevent dementia or cognitive decline in a large long-term RCT.
effect_size: No reduction in incident dementia or Alzheimer's; null on cognitive decline
population: GEM Study, ~3069 adults aged 75+, median ~6 years

provenance.primary: DeKosky et al. - 'Ginkgo biloba for prevention of dementia: a randomized controlled trial (GEM Study)', JAMA 2008

confidence_notes: A clean negative from a large, long, well-powered RCT - the gold-standard refutation of a popular 'brain supplement.' Pairs with mostly-null omega-3 cognition RCTs (e.g. VITAL-COG) to illustrate the predictor-vs-lever gap monetized.
